successors.note: 1887: the French conquest of Senegal ends Sine's independence (Serer people page: "The inter-ethnic wars involving the Serer continued till 1887, when the French colonial forces conquered Senegal"). The Maad a Sinig kept the title through the colonial period as a non-sovereign monarchy and the line ended with Mahecor Joof on 3 August 1969 (Mahecor Joof page: "After his death, the Kingdom of Sine was incorporated into independent Senegal"); the monarchy was restored in 2019. [Fix af-03-x 2026-10-19: the state was held to 1969 and counterpart 'independent Senegal' before.]

Infobox "Established: ca. 1335"; Maysa Wali fled Kaabu "after a battle in 1335" in Gravrand's oral tradition, but "the actual foundation date is unclear" and Becker places the story in 1865-67. The Maad a Sinig page dates the Guelowar kings "between 1350 and 1969". [Fix af-03-x 2026-10-19: counterpart was kaabu, whose dossier starts in 1537; the Guelowar migration from Kaabu is in the page's oral tradition and Kaabu was then a Mali province, so nobody.]

notes:
Sine, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Kingdom of Sine, Kumba Ndoffene Famak Joof, Mahecor Joof, Maba Diakhou Ba (Maad a Sinig reduced to a king list).

No page opened dates the end of Sine's independence: the Sine page is silent, the Kumba Ndoffene Famak Joof page is silent and has only the August 1871 assassination, and the History of Senegal page gives only "the 1850s" for Faidherbe. The state is therefore held to the monarchy's end, 3 August 1969 (Mahecor Joof page), at confidence 2; the real loss of sovereignty fell earlier, probably in the 1880s-1890s, and the french-africa dossier owner should add it as an occupation/protectorate event with a source. The 1335 founding is the infobox date and is questioned by the page. The jolof-empire ledger has Sine absorbed 1390 (bridging) and lost 1520; the Sine page gives no absorption date. Joal (a Sine province) is not drawn.
Gazetteer: Diakhao, Niakhar, Ndok, Fadial, Palmarin, Joal, Fandane-Thiouthioune.

Revised 2026-10-19 after the review (verdict fail): (a) the state now ends in 1887 (c2), the year the Serer people page gives for the French conquest of Senegal; before it was held to 1969 and counterpart 'independent Senegal'. Pages re-read for a Sine-specific date and silent: Kingdom of Sine, Kumba Ndoffene Famak Joof (killed at Joal in August 1871), Maad a Sinig, Mahecor Joof, History of Senegal (Faidherbe 'in the 1850s'), Battle of Fandane-Thiouthioune (1867, no status change). The year is therefore Senegal's, not a Sine treaty; the french-africa owner (af-08) should check it. Maad a Sinig reigns after 1887 (1898-1924 Kumba Ndoffene Fa Ndeb Joof, 1924-1969 Mahecor Joof) are non-sovereign and out of the ruler strip; 1969 is only the end of recognition. (b) The 1520 'gain' from jolof-empire is deleted: Sine was a Jolof vassal (Sine page: 'a vassal of the Jolof Empire'), which jolof-empire records as vassal_start 1390 / vassal_end 1520 cp sine; the shape is Sine's from 1335. (c) The 1335 founding has counterpart nobody (Kaabu's dossier starts in 1537; the Guelowar from Kaabu are oral tradition).
